reading: user-randomised UNDERSTATES the global effect by 55% because 49% of a control user's neighbours are treated and the benefit leaks to them. Cluster randomisation cuts the bias to 30%. Note the SIGN: the marketplace study in interference.py finds the same violation inflating the estimate by 627%. The direction belongs to the mechanism, and a positive-spillover bias is the more dangerous one -- an effect that looks smaller than it is reads as a conservative experiment, and nobody investigates a disappointing result for being too disappointing.
